Pull it out, bury half the plant in soil and keep moist.

Burying it at least halfway up the plant is key. It will develop a stronger root system and result in a stouter plant.

When planting out my seedlings I always bury the whole stem up to the first true leaves for stronger roots.

One season, almost all my plants were downed from high winds, and the tomato stems that were left on the ground (after my lazy clean-up efforts) sprouted roots growing toward the soil anywhere they laid in contact with the ground. Pretty neat to see it in action like that.
